title: Launch Guardian Playbook: Communications, Blocker Gating, and Rollback Coordination
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a single-source 'Launch Guardian' playbook to coordinate release blocker gating, rollback procedures, and incident communications for the runtime-1.22 launch. This document provides clear owner assignments for preflight checks, templates for on-call and customer-facing comms, criteria for abort vs rollback, and a runbook for cross-team decisioning during degraded launches.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook reviewed and signed off by ENG, SRE, Product, and Legal
Three communication templates (on-call escalation, customer advisory, and partner update) stored in Confluence and linked from Console release notes flow
Rollback decision tree validated with simulated dry-run in staging and documented outcomes
A single triage Slack channel and rotation roster configured and verified
All dependencies (ENG-4821, ENG-4999, DES-420) show green or have documented mitigation steps
rollout_checklist: Preflight: run canary traffic against runtime-1.22 in region-us-east-1 (owner: ENG-Canary)
Metrics: ensure latency p95 and error-rate thresholds are being ingested to Console dashboard (owner: Observability)
Capacity: Dedicated pool autoscale verified and burst options tested (owner: Capacity Team)
Docs: release note draft uploaded and validated by UX writer (owner: Product Docs)
Stakeholders: 24h pre-launch readout scheduled with Sales, Support, SRE (owner: PM)
Rollback gates: define threshold breaches that trigger rollback (owner: PM + SRE)
Comms: confirm customer advisory channel list and legal review complete (owner: Legal + PM)
rollback_plan_summary: Two-tier rollback approach: Tier A (fast revert): immediate traffic switch to runtime-1.21 for region(s) exhibiting critical SLO breaches (latency p95 > 2x baseline or error-rate > 3%) — automated router fallback with manual confirmation window. Tier B (controlled rollback): revert config changes, disable feature flags, and open extended incident bridge while preserving degraded service for non-critical workloads. Rollback owners: SRE lead (executes revert), PM (customer comms), Infra Eng (DB/config rollback).
incident_comm_templates: On-call escalation (internal): [<timestamp>] Severity: SEV2. Summary: Observed latency p95 spike to {value} ms in {region}. Impact: increased token cost & degraded UX for streaming endpoints. Immediate actions: pause new canary traffic, capture KV cache stats, escalate to SRE on-call {oncall_name}. Links: <console-metrics-url>, <github-pr>#1234. Owner: SRE

Customer advisory (external): Subject: Service degradation affecting text-generation endpoints in {region}. Body: We are investigating increased latency affecting a subset of requests to the Redwood API. Engineers are actively rolling back a recent runtime change for affected regions while preserving customer data and ensuring security. We will provide a status update within 30 minutes and an estimated time to resolution within 90 minutes. If you require immediate assistance, please contact Support at support@redwood.ai. Owner: PM

Partner status brief: Short summary of impact, expected mitigation path, and action items for partners integrating via Dedicated instances. Include rollback ETA and any required partner-side config changes. Owner: Partner Success
